activity.title: This weekend I got to learn firsthand just how much the Cursor team values students. From day one of the Campus Lead kickoff, we were treated to incredible surprises, gifts, and sneak peeks at upcoming product launches 👀. Through building demos, creating with Cursor, and talking with other leads, I learned a ton about the tool and how people are actually using it. We also built our own keyboards, ate at some amazing spots around the city, and even got to meet investing partners from Dorm Room Fund . If any of this sounds interesting, Jenna Lee and I are working to bring these same experiences to UT. If your club is interested in running an event with Cursor, reach out and let's set something up. #cursor #AITools #UTaustin ...more

Introducing the Fall 2026 class of Cursor Campus Leads. Every AI company is launching a new campus ambassador program right now but this one is going to be different. I wanted to share my summer plans for this year. I'm joining Amazon this summer as a Software Development Engineer (SDE) Intern based in Sunnyvale, California. While in the bay, I'll be participating in Y Combinator’s Startup School. Where I get to engage with the entrepreneurial community and learn about scaling early-stage ventures. I'm super excited for the opportunity to combine technical hardware engineering with entrepreneurial and professional development across two major tech hubs. If you are located in Sunnyvale or Seattle this summer, I'd love to connect. #Amazon #YCombinator #PwC #Internship2026 #Engineering #TechCommunity #StartupSchool ...more

I’m proud to share that out of 25 teams, ours was named runner-up after our final presentation! 🏆 A huge thank you to my teammates , Samik Shah , Jacari Dillard , Navya Mehrotra , Barbie Zhu , and Mauricio Prieto , for making this such a rewarding experience. Our last minute lock in was unmatched. I’m also deeply grateful to our mentors, Phu Nguyen and Rohan A. , whose support and advice carried us through the entire process. We couldn’t have done any of it without y’all! Beyond the competition itself, getting to meet so many MDs, engineers, and fellow students left a really lasting impression. I left knowing fintech is where I want to build my career, at the intersection of markets, technology, and real-world impact. 🏦 #goldman #engineering #Finntech ...more

As promised, here's my full thoughts & opinions on my experience at the Cursor Campus Lead Kickoff this last weekend! Spent three days at the Cursor office in SF with the rest of the Fall 2026 Campus Lead cohort. Huge thank you to Fiona for hosting: somehow ~35 people from schools all over the country actually felt like a community by the end of it. We built keyboards, met with partners from Dorm Room Fund and the founders behind Pointer , Autolab & Neural Motion on a rooftop in SF, and ended up at Insomnia Cookies at hours I will not defend. The best parts were outside the agenda, though. I had some of the most fun swapping notes on what everyone's trying to run on their own campuses this fall, figuring out who's dealing with the same club politics back home, meeting people I'd only ever seen as a LinkedIn name. I'm one of the Cal leads, so over the next few months I'll be bringing some of that energy back to Berkeley – workshops, build nights, collabs with clubs. Club leader at Berkeley looking to collaborate with Cursor to host events for your members and the overall Cal CS/EECS population? Reach out!

Robert W. dropped out of Harvard at 21 with $10,000 in a bank account. Three years later Etched has raised $1B+, is valued over $10B, and has signed $1B+ in customer contracts. He's 24. His explanation for why it worked: "We were absolutely not the best people in the world to solve this. We were the only people willing to." More below in this talk he gave to hundreds of interns.

Really excited to share that SpaceXAI ’s Grok Bot launches today :) I built mine around a cast of South Park characters. Cartman is the orchestration layer, or Chief of Staff. Every morning, he connects to the infrastructure behind my work, queries Databricks, understands the relevant tables and signals, prioritizes the workload, and delegates it to specialist Agents. Kenny handles browser research and monitoring. Stan is trained on my writing voice. Kyle runs smaller, high-context workflows that I taught him through screen recordings, using his own computer instance. It’s no longer how much work I can personally complete. It’s how creatively I can expand the system, connect new sources, and define what Grok Bot should own next. The link to try Grok Bot today is in the comments. SpaceXAI #GrokBot
